ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r1.claim: The majority read the gathering as blind in eyesight, as in another verse; Ibn Atiyya argues that blindness of insight would not be newly felt by unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله أعمى المراد به عمى البصر كما قال ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r2.claim: These interpreters, with a report also from Ibn Abbas, say the person is blind to any argument that could guide him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل وأبو صالح وروي عن ابن عباس: أعمى عن حجته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person is first gathered with sight, then becomes blind upon reaching the gathering place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس يحشر بصيرا ثم إذا استوى إلى المحشر أعمى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r4.speaker: قول آخر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r4.claim: Other explanations say he is helpless to escape punishment, blind to everything but Hell, or unable to find his way; al-Jubbaʾi adopts the last view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r4.anchor: وقيل: أعمى عن الحيلة في دفع العذاب عن نفسه كالأعمى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r5.speaker: إبراهيم بن عرفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r5.claim: Ibrahim ibn ʿArafa says every blameworthy blindness in scripture means blindness of the heart, citing the verse that hearts rather than eyes become blind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r5.anchor: وقال إبراهيم بن عرفة: كل ما ذكره الله عز وجل في كتابه فذمه فإنما يريد عمى القلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the servant’s question as saying he has no defense, although in worldly life he knew and could argue his case.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معنى لم حشرتني أعمى أي لا حجة لي وقد كنت عالما بحجتي

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r5.claim: The apparent contrast with Qāf 50:22 is resolved because people fail to recognize their blindness in earthly life but will recognize it when reality is unveiled at Judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r5.anchor: The answer is that there is no discrepancy.

SAMIN-DURR:20:125/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:125/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:125/r1.claim: The clause وقد كنت بصيرا is circumstantial, describing the object of حشرتني.
SAMIN-DURR:20:125/r1.anchor: جملة حالية من مفعول " حشرتني ". وفتح الياء من

SAMIN-DURR:20:125/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:125/r2.speaker: نافع وابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:20:125/r2.claim: Nafi and Ibn Kathir pronounce the yā in حشرتني with fatḥa before the following hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:20:125/r2.anchor: وفتح الياء من " حشرتني " قبل الهمزة نافع وابن كثير.

ASAD-NOTES:20:125/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:125/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:125/r1.claim: On Resurrection Day the sinner asks why he is blind despite having had sight; God answers that he ignored the divine messages and is now forgotten.
ASAD-NOTES:20:125/r1.anchor: O my Sustainer! Why hast Thou raised me up blind, whereas [on earth]

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.claim: The Qur’an uses ḍank only here as a warning to those who turn from God’s reminder, who will be raised blind.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.anchor: والقرآن لم يستعمل ضنكاً إلا في هذا الموضع، نذيراً لمن أعرض عن ذكره تعالى، يحشره سبحانه يوم القيامة أعمى.

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r1.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r1.claim: Suyuti lists study of verse endings and how each ending suits its verses as one dimension of Qur'anic coherence.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r1.anchor: التاسع بيان فواصل الآى ومناسبتها اللآى التي ختمت بها

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r2.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r2.claim: He includes the relation between each surah's name and its contents among the subjects of coherence.

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r3.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r3.claim: He proposes explaining why the Qur'an chooses one synonym instead of other possible synonyms.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r3.anchor: الحادي عشر بيان وجه اختيار مرادفاته دون سائر المرادفات

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r4.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r4.claim: His method includes famous and anomalous readings, their meanings and knowledge, as one aspect of the Qur'an's inimitability.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r4.anchor: بيان القراءات المختلفة مشهورها وشاذها وماتضمنته من المعاني والعلوم فأن ذلك من جملة وجوه إعجازه

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r5.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r5.claim: He also studies differences among repeated passages, such as additions, omissions, reordered material, or substitution of one word for another.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r5.anchor: بيان وجه تفاوت الآيات المتشابهات في القصص وغيرها بالزيادة والنقص والتقديم والتأخير

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r6.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r6.claim: Suyuti says he made a concise work specifically on coherence in surah order, largely from his own thinking because few had pursued the subject, and selected only views he approved.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r6.anchor: وأكثره من نتاج فكري وولاد نظري لقلة من تكلم في ذلك أو خاض في هذه المسالك

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r7.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r7.claim: He first titled the work Nata'ij al-Fikr, then renamed it Tanāsuq al-Durar because the latter better fit its subject and added wordplay.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r7.anchor: وقد كنت أولا سميته نتائج الفكر في تناسب السورلكونه من مستنتجات فكري

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r8.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r8.claim: Scholars disagree whether surah order came by prophetic instruction or the Companions' independent judgment, while they agree verse order was fixed by instruction.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r8.anchor: اختلف العلماء في ترتيب السور هل هو بتوقيف من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو باجتهاد من الصحابة بعد الاجماع على أن ترتيب الآيات توقيفي

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r9.speaker: مالك والقاضي أبو بكر
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r9.claim: The ijtihad position is held by a group including Malik and Qadi Abu Bakr in one of his two opinions, and Ibn Faris states it decisively.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r9.anchor: فذهب جماعة إلى الثاني منهم مالك والقاضي أبوبكر في أحد قوليه وجزم به ابن فارس

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r10.speaker: جماعة الاجتهاد
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r10.claim: Their evidence is that early codices differed: Ali's followed revelation order, Ibn Mas'ud began with al-Baqara, al-Nisa, then Al Imran, and Ubayy's and other codices also differed.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r10.anchor: ومما استدل به لذلك اختلاف مصاحف السلف في ترتيب السور فمنهم من رتبها على النزول وهو مصحف علي

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r11.speaker: عثمان
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r11.claim: Ibn Ashta transmits through his chain that Uthman ordered the people to place the long surahs together.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r11.anchor: وفي المصاحف لابن أشتة بسنده عن عثمان أنه أمرهم أن يتابعوا الطول

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r12.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r12.claim: The prophetic-order position is held by another group, including Qadi Abu Bakr in his other opinion and many others.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r12.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى الاول منهم القاضي أبو بكر في أحد قوليه وخلائق

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r13.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r13.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains that the whole Qur'an first descended to the lowest heaven, then came down over twenty-odd years; Gabriel showed the Prophet each surah's and verse's place, so their sequence was prophetic and changing it corrupts the Qur'an's order.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p66/r13.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري أنزل الله القرآن كله إلى سماء الدنيا ثم فرقه في بضع وعشرين سنة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r1.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai use imāla in both occurrences of aʿmā, in 20:124 and 20:125.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r1.anchor: أبو بكر عن عاصم (أعمى) و (أعمى) [طه/ 124، 125] مكسورتان

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r2.claim: Hafs from Asim reads both occurrences with fatḥa; Nafi is between imāla and fatḥa, while Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Amir use fatḥa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r2.anchor: حفص عن عاصم بفتحهما. نافع بين الكسر والفتح. أبو عمرو بفتحهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r3.claim: Both imāla and its absence are acceptable here; the author says the matter was discussed earlier.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r3.anchor: الإمالة وتركها جميعا حسنان في هذا، وقد ذكر فيما مر قبل

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r4.claim: Some exegetes take the blindness as inability to see the proof, although the person had seen it in life.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا: أعمى عن الحجة، وقد كنت بصيرا بها

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r5.claim: The phrase may also mean blindness to the paths leading to reward.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أعمى عن طرق الثواب

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

NASHR:v1p13/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p13/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p13/r1.claim: The author rejects requiring tawātur for each individual variant letter: if a reading is established as mutawātir from the Prophet, it must be accepted as Qurʾān whether it agrees with the written rasm or not; demanding this of every variant would eliminate many established readings.
NASHR:v1p13/r1.anchor: فإن التواتر إذا ثبت لا يحتاج فيه إلى الركنين الأخيرين من الرسم وغيره إذ ما ثبت من أحرف الخلاف متواترا عن النبي

NASHR:v1p13/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p13/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p13/r2.claim: The author once leaned toward the strict tawātur condition but later judged it unsound and aligned himself with early and later authorities.
NASHR:v1p13/r2.anchor: وقد كنت قبل أجنح إلى هذا القول، ثم ظهر فساده وموافقة أئمة السلف والخلف

NASHR:v1p13/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p13/r3.speaker: أبو شامة
NASHR:v1p13/r3.claim: Abū Shāma says readings collectively transmitted by the routes and accepted across groups, without objection and with wide circulation, should be treated as mutawātir; at minimum these conditions are required where some lack tawātur.
NASHR:v1p13/r3.anchor: أبو شامة في " مرشده ": وقد شاع على ألسنة جماعة

NASHR:v1p13/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p13/r4.speaker: إبراهيم بن عمر الجعبري
NASHR:v1p13/r4.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī says sound transmission is the sole formal condition, with conformity to Arabic and the rasm necessarily following; knowledge of transmitters, Arabic, and the written codex resolves the issue.
NASHR:v1p13/r4.anchor: الشيخ أبو محمد إبراهيم بن عمر الجعبري أقول: الشرط واحد وهو صحة النقل

QIRAAT-ER:20:125:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:125:4#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:20:125:4#1/r1.claim: The final yāʾ of the first-person object suffix has fatḥa in ḥashartaniya; meaning is unchanged, but the prosodic rhythm differs.
QIRAAT-ER:20:125:4#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Final yāʾ with fatḥa (ḥashartaniya) — an alternate pronunciation of the 1s object suffix

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r1.claim: As before, “he said” begins a new statement after an implied question arising from the preceding account.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r1.anchor: استئناف كما مر ( رب لم حشرتني

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r2.claim: The contrast is with the person’s sight in worldly life; most rejecters had sight, though some were blind from birth.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r2.anchor: أي في الدنيا كما هو ظاهر ولعل هذا باعتبار أكثر أفراد من أعرض

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r3.claim: The question asks what sin earned this punishment; the person is either ignorant of the cause or assumes he committed no deserving sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278/r3.anchor: عن السبب الذي استحق به الحشر لأعمى لأنه جهل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the unbeliever is first resurrected seeing and then blinded; thus “I had been seeing” describes the beginning of resurrection. Al-Alusi says blindness apparently is later removed too.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r5.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه أن الكافر يحشر أولا بصيرا ثم يعمى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r7.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل والضحاك وأبو صالح وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r7.claim: These authorities, in one report from Ibn Abbas, take blindness as lack of proof or insight, and “I had been seeing” as knowing God’s proof and being able to argue in worldly life; Ibrahim ibn ʿUrfa chose this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r7.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد ومقاتل والضحاك وأبي صالح هي رواية عن ابن عباس أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r9.claim: On the insight reading, God says the person was made blind to the argument that could aid him because he abandoned the proofs; as he left them in life, he is left blind forever.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r9.anchor: وحاصل الجواب علية إني حشرتك أعمى القلب لاتهتدي إلى ما يناجيك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf use imala on both occurrences of aʿmā because it is a defective-yāʾ form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف ( أعمى ) بالإمالة في الموضعين لأنه من ذوات الياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r1.claim: The questioner may have been blind in eyesight or blind to the proof.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:125/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:125/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:125/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī apply imāla to both occurrences of aʿmā because the alif derives from yāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:125/r1.anchor: وقد أمالهما حمزة والكسائي لأن الألف منقلبة من الياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:125/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:125/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:125/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr distinguishes the first occurrence because it is at a verse ending and pause position, which favors a change.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:125/r2.anchor: وفرق أبو عمرو بأن الأول رأس الآية ومحل الوقف فهو جدير بالتغيير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r2.claim: Addressing God as Lord recalls prior blessings to elicit mercy, since a benefactor tends to preserve a blessing while there remains room for the recipient's reform.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r2.anchor: أي أيها المحسن إلي المسبغ نعمه علي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r3.claim: Kadhālika may mean that the person acted shamefully in this way in life, or that matters were as he said; the reply then explains the first reading and gives the cause on the second.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r3.anchor: مثل هذا الفعل الشنيع فعلت في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r4.claim: Mujahid says the person's former sight was in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r4.anchor: {قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا} قال: في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r8.claim: Mujahid says the person has no proof for his question.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {لم حشرتني أعمى} قال: لا حجة له

BURSEVI:v5p339/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339/r5.claim: The introductory قال resumes the preceding account as an explanatory answer; Rabb is addressed as Lord.

BURSEVI:v5p339/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339/r6.claim: The question contrasts the person's blindness at resurrection with his sight in worldly life.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r4.claim: Resurrection blindness depicts worldly blindness to guidance and salvation; it marks God's anger and exclusion from mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r4.anchor: تمثيلا لحالته الحسية يومئذ بحالته المعنوية في الدنيا ، وهي حالة عدم النظر في وسائل الهدى والنجاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r5.claim: Blindness in the first instance is figurative, while blindness at resurrection is real.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r5.anchor: فأعمى الأول مجاز وأعمى الثاني حقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r6.claim: The question begins a new sentence, and God's reply is separated because it continues the dialogue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r6.anchor: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى } مستأنفة استئنافا ابتدائيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r13.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r13.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and Hafs from ʿAsim read both occurrences with fatḥa on the two mīms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r13.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم أعمى حشترتني أعمى بفتح الميمين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r14.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r14.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read both occurrences with kasra on the two mīms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r14.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بكسرهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r15.speaker: نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r15.claim: Nafiʿ reads the two occurrences between kasra and fatḥa.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r4.claim: The denier asks why he was gathered blind when he had sight in worldly life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r4.anchor: ولهذا يقول: {رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا} أي: في الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.claim: Some commentators include neglecting Quran recitation, allowing it to be forgotten, and failing to care for it within turning away from God’s remembrance; Ibn Kathir says this is part, though not the whole, of the verse’s intent and is grave negligence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.anchor: وقد أدخل بعض المفسرين هذا المعنى في قوله تعالى: {ومن أعرض عن ذكري

JISHUMI:v7p4761/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r11.claim: The claim that the resurrected person had been sighted does not contradict the verse that his sight is sharp that day; he can be in two different states.
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r11.anchor: فجوابنا: أنه يكون على حالين على ما تقدم

MUJAHID:v1p405/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p405/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p405/r1.claim: The speaker says he had been able to see his proof in worldly life.
MUJAHID:v1p405/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وقد كنت بصيرا ﴾ يقول كنت في الدنيا بصيرا بحجتي

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r9.claim: The speaker is blind to his proof, although he knew it in worldly life.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r9.anchor: هلك عني سلطانيه [الحاقة: 29] يعنى ضلت عنى حجتى

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r10.claim: He links the lost proof to 69:29, interpreting it as my proof has gone from me.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r10.anchor: هلك عني سلطانيه [الحاقة: 29] يعنى ضلت عنى حجتى

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r11.claim: This is said when the person's limbs testify against him for associating partners with God and disbelief.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r11.anchor: وهذا قوله حين شهدت عليه الجوارح بالشرك والكفر.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#2/r1.claim: The resurrected person asks why God gathered him blind when he had sight in worldly life.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا ﴾ في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r1.claim: The speaker asks what sin brought punishment by blindness; his question suggests that he thinks himself guiltless.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r1.anchor: أي بأي ذنب عاقبتني بالعمى. { وقد كنت بصيرا } أي في الدنيا، وكأنه يظن أنه لا ذنب له.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r2.claim: He had been sighted in worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r2.anchor: أي في الدنيا، وكأنه يظن أنه لا ذنب له.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid understand blindness as blindness to his proof, and sightedness as knowing his proof in worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد: أي { قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى } عن حجتي { وقد كنت بصيرا } أي عالما بحجتي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r4.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r4.claim: Al-Qushayri's gloss that the unbeliever knew his proof is far-fetched, Qurtubi says, since an unbeliever had no proof in this world.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r4.anchor: القشيري: وهو بعيد إذ ما كان للكافر حجة في الدنيا.

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r8.claim: One explanation is that God makes the rejecter blind as requital for abandoning and turning away from guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r8.anchor: أنه تعالى إنما أنزل به هذا العمى جزاء على تركه اتباع الهدى والإعراض عنه

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r9.claim: Alternatively, souls that leave their bodies ignorant and disconnected from spiritual beings retain that state, and their spiritual pain intensifies; their worldly rejection of evidence explains the blindness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r9.anchor: هو أن الأرواح البشرية إذا فارقت أبدانها جاهلة ضالة عن الاتصال بالروحانيات بقيت على تلك الحالة

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.claim: Citing a report that a person meets God in the state in which they lived, Qushayri says the worldly blind of heart and the ignorant are resurrected in that condition.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.anchor: في الخبر : ( من كان بحالة لقي الله بها ) فمن كان في الدنيا أعمى القلب يحشر على حالته

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r2.claim: The resurrected ask who raised them from their resting place until knowledge of the truth becomes unavoidable.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r2.anchor: ولذا يقولون : { من بعثنا من مرقدنا } ؟ [ يس : 52 ] إلى أن تصير معارفهم ضرورية

TAB-FULL:v16p201#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p201#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the speaker's question about being gathered blind as saying that he has no argument.
TAB-FULL:v16p201#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، {قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى} [طه: 125] لا حجة لي

TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets I used to see as meaning that the speaker knew his argument.
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، {وقد كنت بصيرا} [طه: 125] قال: عالما بحجتي

TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r2.claim: Another view takes the phrase literally: in worldly life the speaker had sight with which to see things.
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معناه: وقد كنت ذا بصر أبصر به الأشياء

TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r3.claim: In another report, Mujahid says the speaker had physical sight in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {وقد كنت بصيرا} [طه: 125] في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r4.claim: Qatada describes the speaker as far-sighted but short-sighted and blind to the truth.
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا} [طه: 125] قال: كان بعيد البصر، قصير النظر، أعمى عن الحق

TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r5.claim: Al-Tabari says the verse leaves the sense of sight unrestricted: the speaker was blind to his argument and physical sight at resurrection, though he possessed both in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r5.anchor: فتأويل الآية، قال: رب لم حشرتني أعمى عن حجتي ورؤية الأشياء، وقد كنت في الدنيا ذا بصر بذلك كله

TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r6.claim: The question does not deny God's sovereignty: the speaker asks which offense earned this punishment because he thought he had committed no such crime and seeks to know his justly deserved penalty.
TAB-FULL:v16p201#3/r6.anchor: إن ذلك منه مسألة لربه يعرفه الجرم الذي استحق به ذلك، إذ كان قد جهله، وظن أن لا جرم له

TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r4.claim: The question first suggests physical blindness, since it contrasts loss of the sight one had in worldly life; this seems to conflict with passages in which sinners see the terrors and signs of Judgment.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r4.anchor: يسبق إلى الذهن أن عمى يوم القيامة يتعلق ببصر الحس فإن الذي يسأل عنه هو ذهاب البصر

TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r5.claim: To resolve the apparent conflict, some say sinners are first gathered sighted and then blinded; others say they alternate between sight and blindness.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r5.anchor: ذكر بعضهم أنهم يحشرون أولا مبصرين ثم يعمون، وبعضهم أنهم يحشرون مبصرين ثم عميا ثم مبصرين

TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r6.claim: One cannot assume afterlife perception follows worldly rules; a sinner may be blind to felicity and salvation yet see the proof against him, Judgment's terrors, and what intensifies punishment.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r6.anchor: فمن الجائز أن يتبعض الأمر هناك فيكون المجرم أعمى لا يبصر ما فيه سعادة حياته وفلاحه

THALABI:v6p265/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p265/r15.claim: The speaker asks why he was gathered blind despite having previously seen with his eyes.
THALABI:v6p265/r15.anchor: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا بعيني

THALABI:v6p265/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r16.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p265/r16.claim: Mujahid reads the complaint as having known his proof before, but now being deprived of it.
THALABI:v6p265/r16.anchor: بصيرا بعيني، وقال مجاهد: عالما بحجتي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553/r1.claim: The author questions the interpretation “blind to my proof”: he cannot see how a disbeliever could have been clear-sighted about proof when he had no proof in either world.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553/r1.anchor: {قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى} عن حجتي {وقد كنت بصيرا} بها في الدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r5.claim: He asks why God gathered him blind despite his having been able to see.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r5.anchor: { قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا }.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r3.speaker: قتادة والسدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r3.claim: Qatadah and al-Suddi explain the blindness as being without an argument.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r3.anchor: عن الحجة في تفسير قتادة والسدي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r4.claim: The denier had thought himself knowledgeable and able to argue in worldly life, while rejecting what came from God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r4.anchor: في الدنيا، عالما بحجتي في الدنيا، وإنما علمه ذلك عند نفسه في الدنيا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r5.claim: Qatadah says the person was blind to the truth in worldly life.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: عمي عن الحق، أي في الدنيا

DAMGHANI:v1p69/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r6.claim: Baṣīr can mean possessing proof: Moses' interlocutor had proof in worldly life.
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r6.anchor: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا

DAMGHANI:v1p332/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r11.claim: Blindness can mean lacking a proof: the resurrected person is blind to the argument for his punishment.
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r11.anchor: العمى عن الحجة قوله تعالى في سورة طه ونحشره يوم القيامة اعمى يعني عن الحجة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r7.claim: Baṣīr can mean insight into a proof.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r2.claim: Al-aʿmā can mean blind to proof or evidence.

NASHR:v2p322/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r11.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير
NASHR:v2p322/r11.claim: The two Medinese and Ibn Kathir read both yāʾs open in حشرتني أعمى.
NASHR:v2p322/r11.anchor: حشرتني أعمى فتحهما المدنيان، وابن كثير

NASHR:v2p164/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p164/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p164/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū Jaʿfar open the yāʾ in حشرتني أعمى.
NASHR:v2p164/r4.anchor: واتفق ابن كثير ونافع وأبو جعفر على فتح أربع ياءات وهن حشرتني أعمى
